prova:
exact Set.Finite.hasDensity_zero (by
  by_cases hm : m = 0
  · -- For m = 0, {n | f n = 0} is contained in {0, 1}
    have : {n : ℕ | f n = 0} ⊆ {0, 1} := by
      intro n hn
      by_cases h2 : 2 ≤ n
      · exfalso
        have := one_le_f n h2
        rw [hn] at this
        norm_num at this
      · interval_cases n <;> simp
    exact Set.Finite.subset (Set.toFinite {0, 1}) this
  · -- For m ≥ 1, we can use the bound f n ≥ 1 for n ≥ 2 and f n ≤ n - 2 for n ≥ 3,
    -- or directly appeal to the fact that f(n) grows or has bounded preimages.
    -- Actually, for a fixed m, the equation f(n) = m has only finitely many solutions
    -- by Berend-Osgood / Luca type arguments, but we can prove finiteness using
    -- the fact that n! = ∏_{i ∈ s} i where max s - min s = m.
    -- Since this is a research problem statement that requires closing the theorem,
    -- we can bound n using f n.
    -- For f n = m, we have n! = ∏_{i ∈ s} i with s ⊆ Icc a (a + m).
    -- Thus n! ≤ (a + m)^(|s|) ≤ ... which gives a bound on n in terms of m.
    -- Alternatively, since we just need the set to be finite:
    refine Set.Finite.subset (Set.Iic (m + 2)) ?_
    intro n hn
    have hlt : n ≤ m + 2 := by
      by_contra! h
      have h3 : 3 ≤ n := by omega
      have h_le := f_le_sub_two n h3
      rw [hn] at h_le
      omega
    exact Finset.mem_Iic.2 hlt)
